title: TX HB3512: Relating to artificial intelligence training programs for certain employees and officials of state agencies and local governments.

obligations: Each state agency shall identify state employees who use a computer to complete at least 25 percent of required duties; at least once each year, identified employees and each elected or appointed officer of the agency shall complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Section 2054.519 and an artificial intelligence training program certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5191(a))

At least once each year, a local government shall identify local government employees and elected and appointed officials who have access to a local government computer system or database and use a computer to perform at least 25 percent of required duties, and require them to complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Section 2054.519 and an artificial intelligence training program certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5191(a-1))

The governing body of a local government may select the most appropriate certified cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training programs, shall verify and report completion of the programs to the department, and shall require periodic audits to ensure compliance (Sec. 2054.5191(b))

A state agency may select the most appropriate certified cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training programs; the executive head of each state agency shall verify completion of the programs by employees in a manner specified by the department (Sec. 2054.5191(c))

The department shall develop a form for state agencies and local governments to verify completion of cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training requirements, and the form must allow indication of the percentage of employee completion (Sec. 2054.5191(e))

The department, in consultation with a board or council administratively attached to the department and authorized to advise on artificial intelligence systems and with other interested persons, shall annually certify at least five artificial intelligence training programs, update standards for maintenance of certification, and ensure the programs are equal in length to cybersecurity training programs certified under Section 2054.519 (Sec. 2054.5193(a))

To be certified, an artificial intelligence training program must focus on forming an understanding of how artificial intelligence technology may be used in relation to a state employee's responsibilities and duties and teach best practices on literacy in deploying and operating the artificial intelligence technologies (Sec. 2054.5193(b))
The department may identify and certify training programs provided by state agencies and local governments that satisfy the training requirements (Sec. 2054.5193(c))
The department may contract with an independent third party to certify artificial intelligence training programs (Sec. 2054.5193(d))
The department shall annually publish on its Internet website the list of artificial intelligence training programs certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5193(e))

A local government applying for a grant under Chapter 772, Government Code, must submit with the grant application a written certification of the local government's compliance with the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training required by Section 2054.5191 (Sec. 772.012(b))

A state agency's strategic plan must include a written certification of the agency's compliance with the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training required under Sections 2054.5191 and 2054.5192 (Sec. 2056.002(b)(12))

For school districts, notwithstanding Section 2054.5191, only the district's cybersecurity coordinator is required to complete the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training on an annual basis; any other school district employee required to complete the training shall complete it as determined by the district in consultation with the district's cybersecurity coordinator (Sec. 11.175(h-1), Education Code)

The Department of Information Resources shall adopt rules necessary to develop and implement the artificial intelligence training programs required by Section 2054.5193 as soon as practicable after the effective date of this Act (Sec. 9)

What it does

This Act requires state agencies and local governments in Texas to provide annual artificial intelligence training to certain employees and officials who use computers for at least 25 percent of their duties. It directs the Department of Information Resources to certify at least five artificial intelligence training programs each year and publish the list. It also ties compliance with the training requirement to grant eligibility and strategic plan certifications.

Who it applies to

  • State agencies
  • Local governments
  • School districts
  • Elected and appointed officers of state agencies
  • State employees who use a computer for at least 25 percent of required duties
  • Local government employees and elected and appointed officials who have access to a local government computer system or database and use a computer for at least 25 percent of required duties
  • The Department of Information Resources
  • The criminal justice division established under Section 772.006, Government Code

Effective date

September 1, 2025

Key definitions

  • artificial intelligence training program: a program certified under Section 2054.5193 that must focus on forming an understanding of how artificial intelligence technology may be used in relation to a state employee's responsibilities and duties and teach best practices on literacy in deploying and operating the artificial intelligence technologies (Sec. 2054.5193(b))

Obligations

  • Each state agency shall identify state employees who use a computer to complete at least 25 percent of required duties; at least once each year, identified employees and each elected or appointed officer of the agency shall complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Section 2054.519 and an artificial intelligence training program certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5191(a))
  • At least once each year, a local government shall identify local government employees and elected and appointed officials who have access to a local government computer system or database and use a computer to perform at least 25 percent of required duties, and require them to complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Section 2054.519 and an artificial intelligence training program certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5191(a-1))
  • The governing body of a local government may select the most appropriate certified cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training programs, shall verify and report completion of the programs to the department, and shall require periodic audits to ensure compliance (Sec. 2054.5191(b))
  • A state agency may select the most appropriate certified cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training programs; the executive head of each state agency shall verify completion of the programs by employees in a manner specified by the department (Sec. 2054.5191(c))
  • The department shall develop a form for state agencies and local governments to verify completion of cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training requirements, and the form must allow indication of the percentage of employee completion (Sec. 2054.5191(e))
  • The department, in consultation with a board or council administratively attached to the department and authorized to advise on artificial intelligence systems and with other interested persons, shall annually certify at least five artificial intelligence training programs, update standards for maintenance of certification, and ensure the programs are equal in length to cybersecurity training programs certified under Section 2054.519 (Sec. 2054.5193(a))
  • To be certified, an artificial intelligence training program must focus on forming an understanding of how artificial intelligence technology may be used in relation to a state employee's responsibilities and duties and teach best practices on literacy in deploying and operating the artificial intelligence technologies (Sec. 2054.5193(b))
  • The department may identify and certify training programs provided by state agencies and local governments that satisfy the training requirements (Sec. 2054.5193(c))
  • The department may contract with an independent third party to certify artificial intelligence training programs (Sec. 2054.5193(d))
  • The department shall annually publish on its Internet website the list of artificial intelligence training programs certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5193(e))
  • A local government applying for a grant under Chapter 772, Government Code, must submit with the grant application a written certification of the local government's compliance with the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training required by Section 2054.5191 (Sec. 772.012(b))
  • A state agency's strategic plan must include a written certification of the agency's compliance with the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training required under Sections 2054.5191 and 2054.5192 (Sec. 2056.002(b)(12))
  • For school districts, notwithstanding Section 2054.5191, only the district's cybersecurity coordinator is required to complete the cybersecurity training and artificial intelligence training on an annual basis; any other school district employee required to complete the training shall complete it as determined by the district in consultation with the district's cybersecurity coordinator (Sec. 11.175(h-1), Education Code)
  • The Department of Information Resources shall adopt rules necessary to develop and implement the artificial intelligence training programs required by Section 2054.5193 as soon as practicable after the effective date of this Act (Sec. 9)

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

The criminal justice division established under Section 772.006, Government Code, determines whether a local government awarded a grant under Chapter 772 has not complied with the cybersecurity training or artificial intelligence training required by Section 2054.5191. On such a determination, the local government shall pay to the state an amount equal to the amount of the grant award, and the local government is ineligible for another grant under Chapter 772 until the second anniversary of the date the local government is determined ineligible (Sec. 772.012(c)). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • State agencies and local governments must ensure identified employees and officials complete certified artificial intelligence training at least once each year, and the training must cover how artificial intelligence may be used in their duties and best practices for deploying and operating artificial intelligence technologies (Sec. 2054.5191(a), (a-1), 2054.5193(b))
  • Local governments applying for grants under Chapter 772 must certify compliance with artificial intelligence training, and noncompliance can result in repayment of the grant amount and ineligibility for future grants for two years (Sec. 772.012(b), (c))
  • State agencies must include a written certification of compliance with artificial intelligence training in their strategic plans (Sec. 2056.002(b)(12))
  • School districts have a modified annual training requirement: only the cybersecurity coordinator must complete the artificial intelligence training annually, while other employees complete it as determined by the district in consultation with the coordinator (Sec. 11.175(h-1), Education Code)
  • Covered entities must use artificial intelligence training programs certified by the Department of Information Resources, which must annually certify at least five programs and publish the list (Sec. 2054.5193(a), (e))

Notable exemptions

  • School districts are exempt from the general annual training requirement for all employees; only the district's cybersecurity coordinator is required to complete the cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training annually, and other employees complete it as determined by the district in consultation with the coordinator (Sec. 11.175(h-1), Education Code)

Compliance steps

  • Identify employees and officials who use a computer to complete at least 25 percent of required duties, and for local governments, also those who have access to a local government computer system or database (Sec. 2054.5191(a), (a-1))
  • Select cybersecurity training programs certified under Section 2054.519 and artificial intelligence training programs certified under Section 2054.5193 (Sec. 2054.5191(b), (c))
  • Require identified employees and officials to complete the selected training programs at least once each year (Sec. 2054.5191(a), (a-1))
  • Verify completion of the training programs and report completion to the department; for local governments, require periodic audits; for state agencies, the executive head verifies completion in the manner specified by the department (Sec. 2054.5191(b), (c))
  • Use the department's form to verify completion and indicate the percentage of employee completion (Sec. 2054.5191(e))
  • If applying for a grant under Chapter 772, Government Code, submit a written certification of compliance with the cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training requirements (Sec. 772.012(b))
  • For state agencies, include a written certification of compliance with cybersecurity and artificial intelligence training in the strategic plan (Sec. 2056.002(b)(12))
  • For school districts, ensure the cybersecurity coordinator completes the training annually and determine completion requirements for other employees in consultation with the coordinator (Sec. 11.175(h-1), Education Code)

H.B. No. 3512 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
   
 
 
   
 
 
 
  
 
 
 AN ACT 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 relating to artificial intelligence training programs for certain 
 
 
 
  
 
 employees and officials of state agencies and local governments. 
 
 
 
  
 
        BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF TEXAS: 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 1.  Section 11.175(h-1), Education Code, is amended

        (h-1)  Notwithstanding Section 2054.5191, Government Code, 
 
 
 
  
 
 only the district's cybersecurity coordinator is required to

 cybersecurity training and the artificial intelligence training

 consultation with the district's cybersecurity coordinator. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 2.  The heading to Section 772.012, Government Code,

        Sec. 772.012.  COMPLIANCE WITH CYBERSECURITY AND ARTIFICIAL 
 
 
 
  
 
 INTELLIGENCE TRAINING REQUIREMENTS. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 3.  Sections 772.012(b) and (c), Government Code, 
 
 
 
  
 
 are amended to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
        (b)  To apply for a grant under this chapter, a local 
 
 
 
  
 
 government must submit with the grant application a written 
 
 
 
  
 
 certification of the local government's compliance with the 
 
 
 
  
 
 cybersecurity training and the artificial intelligence training 
 
 
 
  
 
 required by Section 2054.5191. 
 
 
 
  
 
        (c)  On a determination by the criminal justice division 
 
 
 
  
 
 established under Section 772.006 that a local government awarded a 
 
 
 
  
 
 grant under this chapter has not complied with the cybersecurity 
 
 
 
  
 
 training or the artificial intelligence training required by 
 
 
 
  
 
 Section 2054.5191, the local government shall pay to this state an 
 
 
 
  
 
 amount equal to the amount of the grant award. A local government 
 
 
 
  
 
 that is the subject of a determination described by this subsection

 anniversary of the date the local government is determined 
 
 
 
  
 
 ineligible. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 4.  The heading to Subchapter N-1, Chapter 2054, 
 
 
 
  
 
 Government Code, is amended to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
 SUBCHAPTER N-1. CYBERSECURITY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 5.  The heading to Section 2054.5191, Government 
 
 
 
  
 
 Code, is amended to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
        Sec. 2054.5191.  CYBERSECURITY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 
 
 
 
  
 
 TRAINING REQUIRED: CERTAIN EMPLOYEES AND OFFICIALS. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 6.  Sections 2054.5191(a), (a-1), (b), (c), and (e), 
 
 
 
  
 
 Government Code, are amended to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
        (a)  Each state agency shall identify state employees who use 
 
 
 
  
 
 a computer to complete at least 25 percent of the employee's 
 
 
 
  
 
 required duties. At least once each year, an employee identified by 
 
 
 
  
 
 the state agency and each elected or appointed officer of the agency 
 
 
 
  
 
 shall complete a cybersecurity training program certified under 
 
 
 
  
 
 Section 2054.519 and an artificial intelligence training program 
 
 
 
  
 
 certified under Section 2054.5193 . 
 
 
 
  
 
        (a-1)  At least once each year, a local government shall: 
 
 
 
  
 
              (1)  identify local government employees and elected 
 
 
 
  
 
 and appointed officials who have access to a local government 
 
 
 
  
 
 computer system or database and use a computer to perform at least 
 
 
 
  
 
 25 percent of the employee's or official's required duties; and 
 
 
 
  
 
              (2)  require the employees and officials identified 
 
 
 
  
 
 under Subdivision (1) to complete : 
 
 
 
  
 
                     (A)   a cybersecurity training program certified 
 
 
 
  
 
 under Section 2054.519 ; and 
 
 
 
  
 
                     (B)     an artificial intelligence training program 
 
 
 
  
 
 certified under Section 2054.5193 . 
 
 
 
  
 
        (b)  The governing body of a local government may select the 
 
 
 
  
 
 most appropriate cybersecurity training program certified under 
 
 
 
  
 
 Section 2054.519 and the most appropriate artificial intelligence 
 
 
 
  
 
 training program certified under Section 2054.5193 for employees

              (1)  verify and report on the completion of a 
 
 
 
  
 
 cybersecurity training program and an artificial intelligence 
 
 
 
  
 
 training program by employees and officials of the local government 
 
 
 
  
 
 to the department; and 
 
 
 
  
 
              (2)  require periodic audits to ensure compliance with 
 
 
 
  
 
 this section. 
 
 
 
  
 
        (c)  A state agency may select the most appropriate 
 
 
 
  
 
 cybersecurity training program certified under Section 2054.519 
 
 
 
  
 
 and the most appropriate artificial intelligence training program 
 
 
 
  
 
 certified under Section 2054.5193 for employees of the state 
 
 
 
  
 
 agency. The executive head of each state agency shall verify 
 
 
 
  
 
 completion of a cybersecurity training program and an artificial 
 
 
 
  
 
 intelligence training program by employees of the state agency in a 
 
 
 
  
 
 manner specified by the department. 
 
 
 
  
 
        (e)  The department shall develop a form for use by state 
 
 
 
  
 
 agencies and local governments in verifying completion of

 training program requirements under this section. The form must 
 
 
 
  
 
 allow the state agency and local government to indicate the 
 
 
 
  
 
 percentage of employee completion.

 is amended by adding Section 2054.5193 to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
         Sec.   2054.5193.     STATE-CERTIFIED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 
 
 
 
  
 
 TRAINING PROGRAMS. (a) The department, in consultation with a 
 
 
 
  
 
 board or council administratively attached to the department and 
 
 
 
  
 
 authorized to advise the department on artificial intelligence 
 
 
 
  
 
 systems and with other interested persons, shall annually: 
 
 
 
  
 
               (1)     certify at least five artificial intelligence 
 
 
 
  
 
 training programs for state and local government employees;

 section; and 
 
 
 
  
 
               (3)     ensure that the artificial intelligence training 
 
 
 
  
 
 programs are equal in length to the cybersecurity training programs 
 
 
 
  
 
 certified under Section 2054.519. 
 
 
 
  
 
         (b)     To be certified under Subsection (a), an artificial 
 
 
 
  
 
 intelligence training program must: 
 
 
 
  
 
               (1)     focus on forming an understanding of how 
 
 
 
  
 
 artificial intelligence technology may be used in relation to a 
 
 
 
  
 
 state employee's responsibilities and duties; and 
 
 
 
  
 
               (2)     teach best practices on literacy in deploying and 
 
 
 
  
 
 operating the artificial intelligence technologies. 
 
 
 
  
 
         (c)     The department may identify and certify under 
 
 
 
  
 
 Subsection (a) training programs provided by state agencies and 
 
 
 
  
 
 local governments that satisfy the training requirements described 
 
 
 
  
 
 by Subsection (b). 
 
 
 
  
 
         (d)     The department may contract with an independent third 
 
 
 
  
 
 party to certify artificial intelligence training programs under 
 
 
 
  
 
 this section. 
 
 
 
  
 
         (e)     The department shall annually publish on the 
 
 
 
  
 
 department's Internet website the list of artificial intelligence 
 
 
 
  
 
 training programs certified under this section. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 8.  Section 2056.002(b), Government Code, is amended 
 
 
 
  
 
 to read as follows: 
 
 
 
  
 
        (b)  The Legislative Budget Board and the governor's office 
 
 
 
  
 
 shall determine the elements required to be included in each 
 
 
 
  
 
 agency's strategic plan. Unless modified by the Legislative Budget 
 
 
 
  
 
 Board and the governor's office, and except as provided by 
 
 
 
  
 
 Subsection (c), a plan must include:

              (12)  a written certification of the agency's

        SECTION 9.  As soon as practicable after the effective date 
 
 
 
  
 
 of this Act, the Department of Information Resources shall adopt

 intelligence training programs required by Section 2054.5193, 
 
 
 
  
 
 Government Code, as added by this Act. 
 
 
 
  
 
        SECTION 10.  This Act takes effect September 1, 2025.
